html:
SMTO-RST-0025 — SMTO couldn't rebuild your saved data from its files

GUID: dc044f4d-cbc2-5e58-9a2f-98ebe63dccb7
Slug: controller-recovery-material-damaged
Domain: RST · Subsystem: controller

What happened

  • SMTO didn't finish starting because some files from your last save are missing or damaged. It kept all of them as they are and didn't switch to an older save on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Don't delete, move or edit anything in SMTO's data folder. Those files are what's needed to recover your most recent saved data.
  2. Note anything unusual that happened recently, such as a power cut, a full disk, or files copied into the data folder by hand. Events like these help the person repairing SMTO find which files were affected.
  3. Open Technical details and select Copy error details. The message names the exact file or part that failed its check.

What success looks like

  • After the repair, the startup screen reaches Ready and your latest conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details and your notes to the person who manages SMTO. Going back to an older save would lose recent work, so only they should decide that. Don't delete the data folder; it holds your conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup recovery could not reconstruct the selected committed revision because its SQLite databases, recovery bundle or required managed files are missing, corrupt or failed integrity checks.

What this means

  • The selected committed revision cannot be reconstructed from its retained SQLite, JSON and required file inventory. Automatic recovery never rolls back or replays operations.

Why this can happen

  • A required file is missing, fails validation or cannot satisfy application record constraints.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Server storage diagnostics and retained manifests without changing committed data.

How to fix it

  • With the Server stopped, preserve the selected generation under the state directory's checkpoints folder and inspect it with python -m agent_runtime.runtime_state.operator inspect on the state root. Repair or restore the missing or damaged SQLite, recovery-bundle or managed-file material for that revision offline; using the previous generation (python -m agent_runtime.runtime_state.operator copy <state root> <new destination> --generation previous) is an explicit rollback decision that discards later work.
  • Preserve the selected generation and recovery evidence. Repair the missing or damaged material offline. An older revision requires an explicit rollback decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • A complete supported representation of the selected revision is available.

How to verify the fix

  • The Server validates the paired representations and reaches READY at the selected revision.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence, automatically roll back or replay commands.

Technical notes

  • Recovery uses the same committed epoch and revision. No model call participates.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-RST-0017 — SMTO couldn't open your saved data safely
